title: SC PSC Order No. 2026-150H — Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Granting Petition to Intervene of Google, LLC - Petition to Establish a Generic Docket for the Purpose of Receiving Comments Addressing Large Load Additions
summary: Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Granting Petition to Intervene of Google, LLC - Petition to Establish a Generic Docket for the Purpose of Receiving Comments Addressing Large Load Additions
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF SOUTH CAROLINA 
STANDING HEARING OFFICER DIRECTIVE 
DOCKET NO. 2026-138-E ORDER NO. 2026-150-H 
JULY 6, 2026 
STANDING HEARING OFFICER: C. Jo Anne Wessinger Hill 
DOCKET DESCRIPTION: Docket No. 2026-138-E -- Petition to Establish a Generic Docket 
for the Purpose of Receiving Comments Addressing Large Load Additions) 
MATTER UNDER CONSIDERATION: Petition to Intervene of Google, LLC (Google) filed 
on June 22, 2026. (Petition to Intervene) 
HEARING OFFICER’S ACTION: This matter comes before the Hearing Officer on the timely 
filed Petition to Intervene of Google, LLC (Google) in this docket. On June 12, 2026, the Clerk’s 
Office of the Commission set the deadline to file a Petition to Intervene in this docket as Monday, 
July 20, 2026. Google seeks to intervene in this proceeding with full rights to participate as a party 
of record. There was no objection filed in this docket opposing the Petition of Google to Intervene 
as provided by S.C. Regs. 103-825A(3). The time for the Applicants or any other party of record 
in this Docket to file an objection or response to the Joint Petition to Intervene has expired. There 
was no Response or objection filed. The Hearing Officer finds that the Petition to Intervene by 
Google is timely filed. 
Having determined that the Petition to Intervene was timely filed, it must next be determined that 
the petitioning party has clear factual support or grounds for the proposed intervention. S.C. Code 
Ann. Regs. 103-825A(3) requires that parties filing a Petition to Intervene in a matter pending 
before the South Carolina Public Service Commission must set forth clearly and concisely: 
(a) The facts from which the nature of the petitioner's alleged right or interest can be
determined;
(b) The grounds of the proposed intervention; and
(c) The position of the petitioner in the proceeding.
The next question to determine is whether the petitioning party or parties state clear factual support 
or grounds for the proposed intervention. 
The Commission opened this generic docket on May 27, 2026, when Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC 
(DEC) and Duke Energy Progress, LLC (DEP) filed a Petition with the Commission. DEC and 
DEP stated that the Petition arises from the Stipulations approved in Commission Orders No. 2025-
757 and 2025-769. The Stipulations adopted by these Orders state that DEC and DEP agreed to 
request ‘that the Commission open a generic docket for the purpose of evaluating issues associated 
with new large load (50 MW or greater) additions’ and ‘request[ing] that the Commission accept 
comments from interested parties’ in this generic docket.” DEC/DEP Transmittal Letter, dated 
May 27, 2026, p. 1. On June 12, 2026, the Commission directed the Chief Clerk to discuss a

DOCKET NO. 2026-138-E 
JULY 6, 2026

procedural schedule with all interested parties so that one can be proposed on June 25, 2026 for 
consideration by the Commission. Order No. 2026-334. Meanwhile, using her administrative 
authority, the Commission Chief Clerk sent a transmittal letter and Notice of Filing directing DEC 
and DEP publish the Notice of Filing, which included the aforementioned deadline to file a Petition 
to Intervene. 

In support of its Petition, Google asserts the following: 

■ 
Google is a “provider of online services and products. In connection with these business 
operations, Google, through its affiliates, is developing one or more data centers and related 
infrastructure in the service territory of Dominion Energy South Carolina (“DESC”).” 
Petition to Intervene, p. 1, ¶ 2. 
■ 
Data Centers are high-load factor facilities that use energy every day, all day. Id., p. 1, ¶ 3. 
■ 
It is critically important to Google’s data center operations to have the availability of an 
adequate and reliable electric power supply at reasonable rates, terms, and conditions. Id., 
p. 1, ¶ 4. 
■ 
Any change or modification to DESC's electric rates and terms of service may have 
material financial impacts on Google’s operations in DESC territory. Id., p. 1, ¶ 5. 
■ 
Google was a signatory, with DESC and other parties of record, to the Large Load 
Stipulation filed in the rate case of DESC (i.e., Docket No. 2025-325-E) and adopted by 
the Commission in Order No. 2026-374. Id., p. 2, ¶ 5. 
■ 
Google has participated in numerous large load dockets throughout the United States and 
is interested in any potential changes to the terms, conditions, and rates for a high energy 
user of DESC like Google. Any changes may have a material financial impact on the 
operations of Google. Id., p. 2, ¶ 7. 
■ 
As a high use customer of DESC with significant economic investment in DESC’s service 
territory, Google has a direct, substantial, and vital interest in the outcome of this 
proceeding. Id., p. 2, ¶ 8. 
■ 
No other party can adequately represent Google’s interest in this matter. Id. 

From the discussion above and assertions in the Petition of Google, LLC, to Intervene, this Hearing 
Officer holds that Google, LLC, has satisfied the criteria for intervention pursuant to Regulation 
103-825A(3) and that clear factual support and/or grounds for the intervention are clearly provided 
and established. No party(s) of record objected to this Petition to Intervene. There is no prejudice 
against the other parties of record. The Petitioner’s interest in these matters can clearly be 
discerned from the Petition. Accordingly, the Petition to Intervene of Google, LLC, is hereby 
granted in this Docket. Google, LLC, is now a formal party of record and it shall actively 
participate in this proceeding with all rights as a party of record. 

This ends the Hearing Officer’s Directive.
